title: Fennel, butter bean and walnut patties

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain staple, such as fennel, tinned butter beans, walnuts, feta, egg, breadcrumbs and yoghurt, with nothing factory-built.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price, with fennel and walnuts both standard lines.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a bowl and a masher, and shaping and frying patties is well within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: Two tins of beans bound with egg and 60g crumbs gives eight firm patties for four, all the filling is already cooked so 4 minutes a side is enough, and the salty feta and lemon keep it well seasoned.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes of prep covers chopping, mashing, shaping and the salad, and 15 minutes of cooking matches 5 minutes softening the fennel plus 8 minutes frying, which suits a quick dinner.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, the fronds come from the listed fennel, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fennel appears twice, cooked in the patties and raw in the salad, which makes it the clear point of a warm September supper alongside late tomatoes.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British instructions, and 'shave' is the only slightly chef-like word, which most cooks will read as slicing thinly.

hearty_healthy.reason: Bean and walnut patties with a fresh fennel and tomato salad and yoghurt make a filling, balanced vegetarian dinner a family would happily repeat.
